findings.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.java:72: canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, allowing administrators with only all-groups view permission to pass requireManage() and create groups; it should require MANAGE.

GroupPermissionsV2.java:123: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates authorization resources instead of realm groups, omitting groups without individual authorization resources covered by all-groups view-members or manage-members grants and causing consuming user-count endpoints to undercount accessible users.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: GroupPermissionsV2.java:123: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates authorization resources instead of realm groups, omitting groups without individual authorization resources covered by all-groups view-members or manage-members grants and causing consuming user-count endpoints to undercount accessible users.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same fundamental issue in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(): the method is incorrectly using authorization resources/resource IDs instead of actual realm group IDs. The golden comment explains the mismatch between hasPermission (which resolves by name/group id) and what's being added to the granted set (resource.getId()), and how this doesn't align with the interface contract expecting group IDs for JPA queries. The candidate comment identifies the same problem - that the method enumerates authorization resources instead of realm groups, which causes groups covered by all-groups permissions to be omitted, leading to incorrect user counts. Both point to the same underlying bug: a mismatch between resource IDs and group IDs that breaks the expected behavior.
